opening.headline: We'll cover the differences between guidelines, memory, and organizational guidelines that keep you from repeating the same explanation with each new conversation, and where it's safe to go.
body: Every time you open a new conversation, you've probably tried explaining yourself again by saying, 'I'm from sales, keep my sentences short.' If there are 20 team members, each of them will repeat the same explanation in a different way. Extending individualized settings across an organization requires other devices.

In this lesson, we'll look at user guidelines that apply to all conversations, memory and chat search (the memories you build from conversations), and organizational guidelines that owners apply to their entire organization. We'll see how the three devices can be turned on, off, and erased, what takes precedence when they collide, and we'll use examples to determine how settings should be different when using it as a personal assistant and when multiple people use the same account.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the differences between user guidelines, memory, and organizational guidelines
Distinguish between when personalization is helpful and when it is dangerous.
It can be explained that instructions and memory are not what the model learned, but rather how stored text enters the request.
Knowing that data usage defaults may be different for personal and organizational plans can help you decide what information you can enter.

screens.title: Repeating the same explanation every time
screens.lead: This is a scene that explains the same background every time you open a new conversation. Read the situation below and consider ways to reduce repetition and its limitations.

visual.alt: A scene where each new chat window has the same background description and several team member icons next to it.
labels: I'm from the sales team. Please keep your sentences short.

paragraphs: An employee on the sales team types the same thing every time he opens AI chat. 'I'm from the sales team, and I'm writing to a customer, so please keep the sentences short.' If you open a conversation five times a day, you're writing the same description five times.

If you look at the team as a whole, the problem becomes bigger. Twenty team members each explain the same standard using slightly different expressions, so even with the same request, the tone of the results varies from person to person. It seems that another device is needed to expand what an individual has set to a standard for the entire organization.

Devices that reduce repetition are as dangerous as they are convenient. You can use it safely by knowing how much information you write down once applies and whose information is mixed in accounts shared by multiple people. The question for this class is this. What is a device to reduce repetition, and to what extent is it safe to use it?

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: It's convenient for AI to remember things about you, but what if those memories are mixed into other people's conversations or accumulated without your knowledge?

screens.outro: Now that we've identified both the repetition problem and the organizational scaling problem, let's think about your setup.

screens.title: Thinking about my AI settings
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think for yourself first and then click.

items.prompt: Have you ever tried opening the Custom Instructions or Memories menu in your app settings?
items.answer: ChatGPT's Custom Instructions are available on all plans on web, desktop, iOS, and Android and are located in the Personalization menu within Settings. Once you set it up for the first time, it will immediately apply to all subsequent conversations. If you've never opened it before, there's still a lot of room for repetition.

items.prompt: Have you ever been surprised by an AI blurting out old conversations?
items.answer: When Memories is turned on, your responses will reflect relevant information from past chats and saved memories. If you're surprised, there are ways to find out where it came from. In this lesson, we'll take a look at where memories come from and how to manage them.

items.prompt: Have you ever worried about your personal information getting mixed up in public accounts?
items.answer: That concern is valid. When multiple people have conversations on an account, one person's preferences and information can be reflected in another person's responses. This is why settings must be set differently for private and public use, and will be explained in detail in the last example.

screens.outro: Let's start with the most basic device: user instructions.

screens.title: Principle of memory: the model contains stored text, not what it has learned.
screens.lead: Select the number marker above the picture to see a detailed explanation. Check out the order in which instructions and memories are stored and how they are communicated to the model.

visual.alt: A flowchart where instructions, memories, and past chats from the app's repository are assembled into a request, through the context window, and into the model.

markers.label: Posts saved by the app
markers.title: Memories are stored outside the model
markers.body: The model itself doesn't remember anything between conversations. Instructions, saved memories, and past chats are texts stored separately by the app. OpenAI Help cites the contents of past chats, saved memories, user instructions, library files, and connected apps as sources of memories. The model does not know me because it learned something new.

markers.label: Request Assembly
markers.title: Pick only the relevant ones and add them to your request
markers.body: When you send a new message, the app selects the saved posts that seem relevant to this response and adds them to the request. OpenAI's help also explains that memory doesn't hold every detail of every conversation, and ChatGPT uses what information it finds relevant to use. So even if there is a memory, it is not reflected every time.

markers.label: context window
markers.title: The text you enter takes up the window.
markers.body: The context window is the limit of tokens the model can read and write in one request. Instructions, memories, this conversation, and new questions all fit into this one window. As the Anthropic Messages API documentation explains, the model continues the conversation by taking the previous conversation turn with each request, so the longer the instructions and memories, the less space there is for the conversation.

markers.label: What this principle explains
markers.title: Understand five results at once
markers.body: First, if you delete a saved post, it will no longer be included in the request and will stop being reflected. Second, instructions and reminders take up space, so keep them short and specific. Third, if multiple people's information is stored in one account, their posts may also be included in other people's requests and mixed in with their responses. Fourth, it is the same principle that organizational guidelines are included in all messages from all members. Fifth, the reason why turning off and deleting is different is also the same. If you turn it off, it will not be included in the request, but the saved posts will remain.

screens.outro: Now that you know the principles, let's start with the most basic user instructions.

ext.title: Anthropic Messages API documentation (pass previous conversation turns as messages with each request)

screens.title: Custom instructions: User instructions that always apply
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare where ChatGPT and Claude set their user guidelines and how they apply them.

visual.alt: Configuration in settings screen showing personalization menu, instructions field and on switch.

tabs.label: ChatGPT
tabs.body:
Custom Instructions is a feature that tells ChatGPT what you want it to consider in your response. Once you set it up, it takes effect in all your conversations immediately, and is available on all plans on web, desktop, iOS, and Android.

On the web and desktop, go to Personalization in Settings and enter the Custom Instructions field. On mobile, do the same in Customize ChatGPT in Settings. Either way, you must turn on the `Enable customization` switch for it to take effect.

Instructions can be modified or deleted at any time and will change from subsequent conversations. Your instructions will not be communicated to anyone who views the shared link. However, if you use a third-party plug-in, the model can provide relevant information in the instructions to the plug-in developer, so you should only use reliable plug-ins and do not enter any information that you do not want to pass on.

tabs.label: Claude
tabs.body:
Claude divides the instructions by scope of application.

**Instructions for Claude** are settings that apply to your entire account. In your settings, write down your preferred approach, common terms, common situations, and general communication style so that they are reflected in all your conversations.

**Project Guidelines** apply only to conversations within a specific project. It is used to determine the project's unique context, work instructions, and roles. Even free accounts can create up to five projects.

Additionally, there are Skills as a separate function that changes the response method, so they must be understood separately from the instructions. The narrower the scope, the less likely it is to impact other conversations, so it's safer to leave criteria for specific tasks in the project guidelines.

tabs.label: common structure
tabs.body:
If you look at the two services in the same framework, three things are the same. First, instructions can be written down once and applied to future conversations without having to be repeated. Second, there is coverage. ChatGPT is divided into all conversations, Claude is divided into account-wide and project-by-project. Third, users can edit and delete it at any time.

The standards for what to write in the instructions are also the same. It is appropriate to repeat content from conversation to conversation, such as roles, writing style preferences, and frequently used terms. Sensitive information such as social security numbers or account information is not included in the instructions. Because guidelines are information that accompanies every conversation.

screens.outro: Now that you've seen the instructions, let's look at memories, which are memories that build up spontaneously from conversations.

screens.title: Memory and chat retrieval
screens.lead: Select the arrows to move through each step to see where your memories are gathered and how you can check, edit, and turn them off.

visual.alt: Management flow chart from memory source list through memory summary to edit, turn off and delete.

steps.title: source of memory
steps.body: When turned on, ChatGPT's Memory remembers relevant preferences and details to help you continue your work. Sources vary by plan and region, but may include past chats, saved memories, Custom Instructions, library files, and content from connected apps like Gmail. Remember that the source contains the connecting app.

steps.title: don't remember everything
steps.body: Memory doesn't keep every detail of every conversation. Among the available information, the model determines and uses what is relevant to the response, and memory changes as the user's context changes. So, even if you have a memory, it doesn't always reflect the information you want.

steps.title: Check with memory summary
steps.body: A memory summary is a high-level view of the information that ChatGPT can use to personalize your response. Please note that the summary does not include all details and sources. You can also ask ChatGPT directly what it remembers, and check which past chats or memories were used when the source appears below the response.

steps.title: Edit, reduce mention, delete
steps.body: The summary allows you to do three things: This includes correcting incorrect information in the input window, 'Do not mention again', which prevents specific information from being mentioned in the future, and 'Delete and turn off', which erases the memorized information and turns off the memory. ‘Don’t mention it again’ only reduces future mentions and doesn’t delete the original.

steps.title: Turning off and erasing are different
steps.body: Turning off Memory will not delete past chats. If you turn it back on later, new memories can be created from the remaining conversation history. To completely get rid of it, you have to erase the record itself. Delete and Turn off erases the memories shown in the summary but leaves past chats intact.

steps.title: Search Claude's Chat
steps.body: Claude's Chat Search is a feature that allows you to find and reference previous conversations on paid plans such as Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. The search scope is divided into all conversations outside of a project, and conversations within each project. Within a project, only conversations within that project are searched. You can stop this feature by turning off the 'Search and reference chats' toggle in Memory in Settings, which will guide you through how to exclude secret chats from searches.

screens.outro: Now that we've covered how to manage memory, let's move on to guidelines that apply to the entire organization.

screens.title: Organizational Guidelines: Apply the same standards across teams
screens.lead: Switch between the two states to compare the results of the same request with and without organizational guidance.

visual.alt: A diagram showing two layers of organizational and personal guidelines overlapping each other, with the upper layer winning when they collide.
labels: Organizational Guidelines (set by owner, apply to all members)
Personal instructions (only you can view and edit)
In case of conflict, the top takes precedence
Personal guidelines apply to areas not covered by the organization.

states.label: Personal instructions only
states.body:
Unless the owner sets separate organizational guidelines, members follow their own personal guidelines. If a member writes, ‘Always give very detailed answers,’ the response will be lengthy in all of that member’s conversations. If another member wrote 'succinctly', the response would be short.

This is why the tone and length of the request vary from person to person even when making the same request. If the team has to deliver the same look to the customer, the standards can be scattered in this state.

Personal guidelines can only be viewed and edited by you, and apply only to that person's conversations.

states.label: Organizational Guidelines + Personal Guidelines
states.body:
Claude's organization guidelines are set by owners of Team and Enterprise plans and apply to all conversations in their organization. We write about content that needs to appear everywhere, such as communication standards, formatting requirements, compliance guidance, and sector-specific context. Organizational guidelines can only be viewed and modified by the owner or higher, and personal guidelines can only be viewed and modified by the owner.

If the two conflict, organizational guidelines take precedence. As in the example in the article, if the organizational guideline is 'Always answer in formal English' and the personal guideline is 'Answer in a relaxed tone of voice', Claude answers formally. Where organizational guidelines do not cover, individual guidelines apply.

Organizational guidelines can be up to 3,000 characters long and are included in all messages from all members, so they should be concise and specific. Priorities rely on prompt-level instructions, so in rare cases of conflict, the behavior may vary, so it is recommended to set them and check whether the desired results are obtained.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen all three devices, let's organize the setup into the same framework.

screens.title: Comparison of setting structure with turning off/deleting personalization
screens.lead: Each row in the table shows where and how ChatGPT and Claude cover the same topic. Read horizontally and check out the common structures.

data.caption: Comparison of personalization settings structures between ChatGPT and Claude
rows: Custom Instructions under Personalization in Settings. Turn on and off with the `Enable customization` switch
Instructions for Claude (account-wide) and Project Instructions (dialogue within the project) in Settings
Memory of personalization. Sources may include content from past chats, saved memories, instructions, files, and connected apps.
Memory settings. Remembers the context of previous conversations and can bring them into new conversations
Control items such as Reference chat history
Chat search on paid plans. Turn off the 'Search and reference chats' toggle in Memory in Settings.
Team and Enterprise owners set organizational guidelines, and in case of conflict, organizational guidelines take precedence
In the Memory summary, select Modify, Never Mention Again, or Delete and Turn Off. Even if you turn off Memory, past chats are not deleted.

data.notes: Turning it off and deleting it are different. Off stops you from using the feature, and Delete removes any saved memories or records. For example, even if you turn off Memory, past chats remain, so if you turn it back on later, new memories can be created from those records. Additionally, ChatGPT help informs you that even if Memory or personalization is turned off, using limited context for safety and security in rare and high-risk situations is separate from personalization control. Therefore, if you want to completely erase the memory, you must check for deletion from the summary or even the deletion of the record itself. The name of the settings menu may look different depending on the plan, region, and screen, so search by role rather than name.

screens.outro: Now that we've organized the structure, let's judge the setup using two examples.

screens.title: Case Commentary 1: Personalization for personal assistant use
screens.lead: The instructor explains the process of determining a setting for use as a personal assistant where a person keeps his or her schedule and writing style. Select the arrows and follow them step by step.

steps.title: situation
steps.body: An employee's role, schedule management style, and writing style preferences will continue to be reflected in AI. The account is only for you, and most of your conversations are about your work.

steps.title: Why it helps
steps.body: In this situation, personalization gives two things. The repetition of background explanations for each dialogue is reduced, and the writing style and format remain consistent. Memory helps you carry on from previous conversations and reduces the time you spend repeating yourself.

steps.title: settings
steps.body: Write your role and writing style in Custom Instructions. For example, ‘I am an assistant manager of the sales team, and I write short sentences when sending messages to customers.’ Then turn on Memory to let repeated preferences accumulate naturally.

steps.title: caution
steps.body: Sensitive personal information is not stored in instructions or memories. Since the source of the memory can also include the contents of the connected app, we also check what the connected app is. If you use a third-party plugin, also consider that the information in the instructions may be passed on to the developer.

steps.title: Storage and learning: standards for information that can be stored
steps.body:
Whether conversations are saved and used to improve models varies by service and plan. Just remember the structure.

Personal plans often have a setting that allows you to choose whether conversations should be used to improve the model. ChatGPT informs you that if you turn off the 'Improve the model for everyone' setting in Data controls in Settings, new conversations will not be used for learning, but turning this setting off will not erase saved conversations. Anthropic informs that personal product conversations can be used if the user allows model improvement, etc., and explains that secret chat is not used regardless of the permission setting. The Gemini app informs you that your activity storage settings determine whether conversations are saved to your activity and can be used to improve the service.

Organizational plans have different defaults. OpenAI explains that it does not use work data from ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and API platforms for learning, and Anthropic also explains that it does not use input and output from Claude for Work and API for learning. However, there are exceptions, such as when the user explicitly sends information, such as through the feedback button.

So, I first check the data policy of the plan I am using to determine what information I can enter. Your personal and organizational plans may have different defaults, and either way, it's safest not to include any sensitive information in the first place.

steps.title: Inspection and correction
steps.body: Occasionally open the memory summary to see what you remember. Edit or delete any memories that were left incorrectly in the summary, and write 'Do not mention again' for information that you do not want to be mentioned in the future, but remember to keep the original. If you make this review a habit about once a month, you can reduce unexpected mentions or reflections of old information that occur as memories quietly accumulate. To enjoy the long-term benefits of personalization in your personal assistant, inspection is as important as setting.

screens.outro: Now that we've finished using it for personal use, we'll explain why it should be set up differently for your team's public account.

screens.title: Case Commentary 2: Why are settings different in team public accounts?
screens.lead: Switch between the two states to compare what you turn on and off in your personal assistant and team shared accounts.

states.label: personal assistant
states.body:
If you use your account alone, the place where your memories are stored and the person who uses it are the same. So it pays to turn on personalization.

**What to turn on:** Write down your role and writing style in Custom Instructions. Turn on Memory to carry over your preferences from previous conversations. If you use Claude, turn on chat search to find and continue past discussions.

**Items to check:** Open and check the memory summary periodically, and correct or delete incorrect memories. Sensitive personal information is not stored in instructions or memories from the beginning.

In personal assistants, the risk of personalization is mainly limited to the user's own information management issues, so there are great benefits to just checking habits.

states.label: Team public account
states.body:
Assume a situation where multiple people share one account. The danger here is that one person's preferences and information become stored in memory and mixed into the other person's responses. Customer information entered by a sales representative may be reflected in responses from other employees in conversations.

The source of the memory may also include content from connected apps, which may lead to unintended exposure. For example, the content of one person's linked mail may affect another person's response.

**Turn off:** Turn off personalization and memory. Turn off chat search if you don't need it.

**Alternative device:** Common standards are based on organizational guidelines established once by the owner. Organizational guidelines apply to all members on the same basis, can only be modified by the owner, and are written concisely within 3,000 characters.

The conclusion is this: Personal assistants turn on personalization, and public accounts are designed around organizational guidelines.

screens.outro: Now that we've finished the case, let's summarize the main points of this lesson.

screens.title: Reduce repetition but set boundaries
screens.lead: Let's organize the three devices covered in this class by connecting them to the first question.

paragraphs: The first question was what device to reduce repetition is and to what extent it is safe to use. There are three devices: I personally write user guidelines and apply them to all conversations. Memory and chat search leverages the memories you build from your conversations. Organizational guidelines ensure that owners apply the same standards to the entire team.

The criteria for safety are coverage and manageability. The instructions are not to write down sensitive information because what you write will follow every conversation. Memories can be sourced and incorrect memories can be corrected or erased. Also remember that turning it off and deleting it are different. Organizational guidelines take precedence when they conflict with personal guidelines, so write concisely and confirm the behavior after setup.

Lastly, the decision depends on the intended use. Personalization is helpful for personal assistants used by one person, but there is a risk of memories being mixed up in public accounts shared by multiple people, so turn off personalization and establish common standards as organizational guidelines.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: The greater the convenience, the more you check the coverage first. The first safety question is whose conversation this applies to.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: This response reflects the preference for apps with memory turned on, as indicated in previous conversations. What most accurately describes this process?
options: Through the conversation, the model relearned itself and remembered me.
The app selected relevant articles from the saved articles and placed them in the context window of this request.
The model learned my preferences from other users' conversations
Context window limits disappear when memory is turned on
checks.explain: The model doesn't remember anything between conversations. The app inputs relevant information from the stored instructions and memories into the request, and the text occupies the context window.

wrong.0: Instead of the model being retrained for each conversation, saved text is fed into the request.
wrong.2: One user's memories going to another user is a risk of sharing accounts, and it's not something the model finds out.
wrong.3: Saved posts also occupy the window, so the limit remains the same, but writing space is reduced.

checks.q: I turned off Memory in ChatGPT. What is the correct explanation at this time?
options: All past chats are deleted and cannot be restored even if you turn them on again.
Only saved memories remain and Custom Instructions disappear together.
Past chats are not deleted, and when you turn them back on, new memories can be created from the remaining history.
The moment you turn it off, the connected app contents are deleted from your account.
checks.explain: Turning off means you stop using it, not deleting it. Past chats remain so you can create new memories when you turn them back on.

wrong.0: Turning off Memory will not delete past chats.
wrong.1: Custom Instructions is a separate setting from Memory.
wrong.3: Turning off does not clear data from connected apps.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: In Claude's team, the organizational guideline set by the owner is ‘Answer concisely’, and one member’s personal guideline is ‘Always answer in great detail.’ What response will this member receive?
options: Personal instructions take precedence, so always answer in great detail.
Organizational guidelines take precedence, and individual guidelines apply to areas not covered by the organization.
Two guidelines conflict so neither guideline applies
Each member chooses which guidelines to use each time.
checks.explain: In case of conflict, organizational guidelines take precedence, and personal guidelines apply to any areas not covered by organizational guidelines.

wrong.0: It is a common misconception that personal guidelines take precedence over organizational guidelines.
wrong.2: Conflicting does not invalidate all instructions and there are rules of precedence.
wrong.3: It is not a structure that the user chooses every time, but is determined by priority.

Public account where multiple people share the same account

When you want to erase the stored memory itself

glossary.def: Customized guidelines for each user that apply to every conversation. You can edit or delete it at any time.
This function remembers relevant information from past conversations and reflects it in the response. You can edit or delete it from the summary.
This is a function to find and reference previous conversations. At Claude it is available in paid plans and can be turned off with a toggle.

These are guidelines that Team and Enterprise plan owners apply to conversations across their organizations. If there is a conflict with personal guidelines, organizational guidelines will take precedence.
This is the limit on how many tokens the model can read and write in a single request. Instructions, memories, and conversations all share this one window.
This is a setting that allows you to choose whether to use your conversation to improve the service model. Your personal and organizational plans may have different defaults.

misconceptions.myth: When you turn off memory, past conversations are erased.
misconceptions.fact: Turning off means you stop using it, not deleting it. Your past chats will remain, and new memories can be created from those records when you turn them back on.

misconceptions.myth: Personal guidelines take precedence over organizational guidelines.
misconceptions.fact: If two guidelines directly conflict, the organizational guidelines will take precedence. Where organizational guidelines do not cover, individual guidelines apply.

misconceptions.myth: If you click ‘Don’t mention this again’, your original memory will be erased.
misconceptions.fact: This choice only reduces future mentions and does not delete the original. To clear it, you must select Delete.

misconceptions.myth: The AI model automatically remembers my conversations.
misconceptions.fact: The model itself doesn't remember anything between conversations. Requests contain instructions and memories stored by the app, and if you clear them, they will no longer be reflected.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Custom instructions are user-specific instructions that apply to all conversations.
Memory and chat search are managed by editing, turning off, and deleting. Turning off and deleting are different.
Organizational guidelines are set by the owner and take precedence if they conflict with personal guidelines.
Personalization is helpful for personal assistants, but public accounts risk mixing up memories, so they are designed around organizational guidelines.

Memory and instructions are not what the model has learned, but rather text that the app saves and inserts into the request. Since the storage and learning policy is different for each plan, check the policy before entering the information.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Among the things I explain over and over again, which are the things I should write down in my instructions and which ones I should never write down?
